Where $\mathcal{I}_i$ is the integral of transmittance over segment $i$ [S1].

The claim states that $I_i$ is the integral of transmittance over segment $i$. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly defines the conditional probability as $P(x|x in [t_{C,i-1}, t_{C,i}]) = T'_i / T_i = e^{-sigma_t(x+d_m(x))} / T_i$. In this equation, the numerator $e^{-sigma_t(x+d_m(x))}$ represents the transmittance at point $x$, and the denominator $T_i$ represents the integral of this transmittance over the segment (as implied by the ratio being a probability density normalized over the segment). Furthermore, the final PDF equation uses $I_i$ in the denominator of the conditional term ($I'_i(x)/I_i$), consistent with $I_i$ being the integral of the transmittance component over segment $i$. Thus, the evidence supports the definition.
